draft.title: Drought
card: A drought is a long period of below-average rainfall. One dry week or one dry month is not a drought.
A drought builds slowly, over months or years. It often has no clear start or end, unlike a flood or a storm.
Soil dries out and dams, rivers and groundwater run low. Crops fail, farm animals go short of feed and water, and plants can die.
Towns can be hurt too. Water use may be restricted, and businesses that depend on farmers may lose income.
draft.remember: A drought is a slow build-up of dry weather that dries out land and water supplies.

a.q: Which description best fits a drought?
opts: Months of below-average rain that dry out soil and dams
A week of heavy rain that makes a river burst its banks
A single hot day when no rain falls on a town
A sudden storm that brings strong winds and big waves
a.why: A drought is a long period of below-average rainfall that slowly dries out the land. A single hot day is too short to be a drought, and a storm or flood is sudden.
a.clue: Think about how long the dry weather lasts and how fast it builds.

b.q: Over two years, a wheat farming district near Geraldton in Western Australia gets much less rain than usual. Dams are almost empty. Which is the most likely effect on the district?
opts: Crops fail and farmers have less income
Paddocks are covered by floodwater for weeks
Strong winds tear the roofs off many houses
Rivers rise quickly and wash away bridges
b.why: Long, below-average rainfall dries out soil and dams, so crops fail and farm income falls. Floodwater, strong winds and rising rivers come from too much rain or from storms, not from a drought.
b.clue: The rain was far below normal for two years.

a.best: Months of below-average rain that dry out soil and dams

b.best: Crops fail and farmers have less income
